title: Turn an idea for a meal into a clear booking
intro: If you are wondering how to book a private chef in Dubai, start with the occasion or routine you want help with. You do not need a finished menu to make a useful enquiry. Dates, location, guest count, preferred style and essential dietary requirements give myCHEF a foundation for discussing options. From there, the conversation moves towards a suitable chef, practical service plan and written proposal. The sections below explain the decisions that make that process easier and help you arrive at the day knowing what has been arranged.

sections.title: Bring your priorities; we will discuss the practical shape
paragraphs: You may know exactly which cuisine you want, or simply that you would like to spend more time with your guests. Both are useful starting points. Explain what matters most and what you would like the team to handle, including any table setup or service support.

The next step is to connect those wishes with the kitchen, timing and budget. Review the proposed menu and responsibilities together before confirming. A clear booking gives you confidence in the arrangement and gives the chef the information needed to prepare for your home or occasion.

sections.title: Send a brief that makes the first proposal useful
paragraphs: A useful enquiry can be short and still contain the essentials. Include your Dubai location, preferred date or start date, number of people, the meals you need and any essential dietary requirements. Add whether the service is a recurring household arrangement or a one-off occasion, because those lead to different menus, staffing and pricing discussions.

Then describe what a successful result would feel like. Perhaps you want dinner ready when you arrive home, a fridge organised for several busy days or a celebration where you can stay with your guests. This helps the team recommend a suitable format instead of making you choose from options that do not address your main priority.

If you have a budget in mind, share it with the scope. That creates a practical starting point for discussing the number of courses, frequency or staffing. An enquiry begins a conversation; the final menu, availability, responsibilities and price are confirmed in the written booking details.

link.label: Share your chef or dining brief

sections.title: Plan arrival time around preparation, not just mealtime
paragraphs: The time you want to eat is different from the time the chef needs to arrive. Ingredients may need preparation, several dishes may need different cooking stages and the table may need attention before guests sit down. Give the team your preferred meal time and ask for an arrival schedule that reflects the agreed menu.

For recurring visits, consider when the kitchen is busiest. Breakfast routines, school departures, deliveries and household staff schedules can all affect access to the workspace. A sensible start time allows the chef to work comfortably while keeping disruption to your household low. If you work from home, mention rooms or periods that need to stay quiet.

Also confirm when the service is expected to finish and what happens if plans run late. Additional tasks or extended service may require more time and an extra charge under the agreed terms. Raising these possibilities before the day is easier than trying to negotiate them while a meal is already underway.

link.label: Compare service types and booked hours

sections.title: Help your chef understand the kitchen before arrival
paragraphs: A few practical details can make the first cooking day much smoother. Share the type of hob, oven capacity, available fridge space and any equipment the chef should know about. Photographs of the working area can help when the kitchen is unfamiliar. A small, well-organised kitchen can support excellent food when the menu is designed around it.

Discuss any specialist requirements before approving a dish. A menu that depends on several oven temperatures at once, a large freezer or equipment you do not own may need to be adapted. The aim is to choose food that can be cooked and served confidently in your actual home, within the agreed time.

Set aside preparation space and make essential utensils accessible. Let the chef know about delicate surfaces, appliances with unusual controls and items reserved for specific dietary needs. Confirm what cleanup includes as part of the booking, so the end of the visit is as well organised as the beginning.

link.label: Prepare for your first cooking day

sections.title: Compare what the price includes, line by line
paragraphs: Two chef quotes can look similar while covering very different work. One may include only cooking time; another may include shopping, an assistant or a longer period of service. Compare the booked hours, number of meals, guest count and responsibilities before deciding which proposal represents better value for your needs.

Keep groceries, equipment and hospitality visible in the comparison. Ask whether the figure includes applicable VAT and which optional items are priced separately. If the proposal refers to a recurring period, check the number of visits rather than assuming every calendar month contains the same service days. The pricing calculator can help you compare a starting arrangement, but the written scope confirms the booking.

A clear quote also explains what would change the total. Additional guests, a more elaborate menu, extended hours or extra staffing can all affect the work involved. Agree how changes are approved so you can make decisions with a clear understanding of the price.

sections.title: Confirm the practical details before the date is secured
paragraphs: A promising menu is only one part of a booking. Before confirming, review the date, address, guest count, arrival time, service hours and included roles. Make sure the dietary brief and any essential equipment requirements are reflected in the proposal rather than left in separate messages that can be overlooked.

Read the payment schedule and the terms that apply to your particular service. A recurring household plan and a one-off event may have different arrangements for changes, cancellation and outstanding balances. Use the terms attached to your booking rather than assuming a policy from another service or an earlier quotation automatically applies.

Keep one agreed version of the menu and scope. If you change the number of guests, request a new dish or move the meal time, ask for confirmation of any effect on staffing, availability and price. This creates a clear reference for you and the team and helps the chef prepare for the service you actually expect.

link.label: Read the private client booking terms

sections.title: Make the first visit a useful foundation
paragraphs: For the first visit, choose a menu that gives the chef a realistic picture of your household. Include food you know well enough to give useful feedback on, rather than making every dish unfamiliar. Keep the priorities clear: which meal matters most, what should be prepared for later and what time the kitchen needs to be ready.

Allow a short introduction to the space. Show the chef the appliances, utensils, storage areas and any items that need special care. Confirm the grocery arrangements and clarify which household member should answer questions if you are unavailable. This helps prevent small uncertainties from interrupting the cooking repeatedly.

At the end, review the practical handover as well as the food. Know which dishes are ready to eat, which need finishing and what instructions apply to them. Then share feedback on portions, taste and timing. The first visit is an opportunity to make the next one more precise, comfortable and useful for everyone involved.

cta.title: Let’s shape the details around you.
cta.body: Share your date or preferred cooking schedule, Dubai location and the number of people you are planning for. Tell us what you would most like help with, and we will discuss a suitable menu and service arrangement before confirming the details in writing.
